mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 4% in the month preceding the forecast period leads to a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding expected equity cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.0% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from a pre-tightening baseline (p > 0.10) during periods where FEDFUNDS > 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in employment (PAYEMS) of at least 20,000 jobs coinciding with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.0% predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as labor market strength supports equity risk appetite.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS month-over-month increase ≥ 20,000 AND UNRATE month-over-month decline < -0.5 percentage point
regime_hint: Labor market strengthening in expansionary regime
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns under trigger conditions are not statistically positive (p > 0.10) after controlling for sector-specific volatility.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly rise in industrial production (INDPRO) by at least 5% followed by a month-on-month decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2.0% predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as a leading indicator of balanced demand growth and cooling price pressures.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO month-over-month increase ≥ 5% AND CPIAUCSL month-over-month decrease < -0.5%
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns under trigger are negative or flat (p > 0.10) in out-of-sample tests.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) of at least 8% in two consecutive months signals supply-side weakness that precedes a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return as investors anticipate near-term earnings compression.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO month-over-month decline ≥ -8% for two consecutive months
regime_hint: Supply shock or demand destruction episode
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during confirmed supply contractions.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2.0% for three consecutive months in a non-recessionary economy predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as expectations of lower future rate hikes improve equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL month-over-month decline < -0.5% for three consecutive months AND GDP growth > 1% in prior quarter
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns under trigger are not statistically positive (p > 0.10) after adjusting for sector-specific macroeconomic risk.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden jump in job openings (HOUST) exceeding 1.5 million units in a month while unemployment remains below 4.0% predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as labor market imbalances signal strong demand.
candidate_trigger: HOUST month-over-month increase ≥ 1,500,000 AND UNRATE month-over-month decline < -0.2 percentage point
regime_hint: Labor market imbalances in expansionary phase
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns under trigger are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) after controlling for sector-specific news.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly rise in retail sales (not available in provided proxies; fallback to GDPC1 as a proxy for broad demand) of at least 3% followed by a decline in mortgage applications (not available; fallback to no additional proxy) predicts a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return as over-heating demand risks a pullback.
Note: GDPC1 is used as a proxy for aggregate demand due to missing retail sales series in the provided catalog.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 month-over-month increase ≥ 3% AND (no additional proxy available for trigger)
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.10) during periods of strong GDPC1 growth.

mechanism_narrative: In a deflationary regime (CPIAUCSL < 200 for two consecutive months), a subsequent rise in consumer sentiment (not available; fallback to a regime-based trigger using UNRATE and HOUST) predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as risk aversion declines during economic uncertainty.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL month-over-month decline < -2% for two consecutive months AND UNRATE month-over-month decline > -0.4% AND HOUST month-over-month increase > 100,000
regime_hint: Deflationary regime as defined by CPIAUCSL
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns under regime trigger are not statistically positive (p > 0.10) in out-of-sample regime-identified windows.
